structure:
Part 6 read, in full, the 12 flat animals feature specs that cover what happens to a notification after it is submitted and who may see it: tests/animals/e2e/features/amend-endings.spec.ts (205 lines, 12 tests), cancel-amend-ui.spec.ts (150 lines, 8 tests), auth.spec.ts (93 lines, 10 tests), amend-from-a-later-session.spec.ts (52 lines, 3 tests), amend-review-title.spec.ts (43 lines, 2 tests), amend-resubmit.spec.ts (44 lines, 1 test), declare-stale-notification.spec.ts (53 lines, 2 tests), notification-delete.spec.ts (27 lines, 2 tests), organisation-scoped-notifications.spec.ts (47 lines, 3 tests), organisation-scoped-notification-page.spec.ts (27 lines, 1 test), admin-visibility.spec.ts (24 lines, 1 test) and commercial-transporter-submission.spec.ts (37 lines, 1 test): 46 tests in all. Since the earlier extract, amend-endings.spec.ts lost its contact address checks (the contact address page ending while amending, and Cancel amend from it) and the commercial transporter submission no longer passes through the contact address task, so those claims are dropped. It also read the support files the partition names: page-objects/animals/{notification-view-page, notification-cancel-amend-page, delete-notification-page, dashboard-page, overview-page, declaration-page, confirmation-page, commercial-transporter-page}.ts, page-objects/shared/{view-header, delete-notification, govuk-banners, page-not-found}.ts, page-objects/shared/auth/{sign-in-page, sign-out-page, sign-in-error-page, organisation-picker-page}.ts, domain/animals/models/api/notification-status.ts, flows/animals/{notification-actions, seeded-journey}.ts, fixtures/{auth-state, ui}.ts and config/users.ts. Where a spec's wording rests on a file the partition does not name, that file was opened for the verbatim string only: page-objects/shared/base-page.ts (the journey strip, status tag, Cancel amend, page-ending controls, sign-in retry and organisation picker handling), page-objects/shared/sets.ts, page-objects/shared/dashboard-copy.ts, page-objects/shared/journey-checks.ts, adapters/http/{organisation, expect-api-refusal}.ts, domain/animals/constants/transporters.ts and the flows/animals/journey.ts methods the specs call (saveAndContinueStopsFrom, openReviewFromOverview, uploadScannedDocument, fillAndSaveCommercialTransporterAddFormToOverview).

It covered, as claims: how an amend starts (from the dashboard card, in the same session and in a later one) and how it is refused on a deleted notification; what the amend review's heading and page title read before and after an answer changes, and that a document upload alone does not change them; every page ending the specs pin while amending (from Overview, on origin, CPH number and permanent address), the Change-link trails and the Save-and-continue walk back to the review; the refused amend review and its error summary; the cancel amendment confirmation page as a page with its heading, body sentence, two buttons and status bar, and every ending cancelling is proven to reach, with and without JavaScript; resubmission back to Submitted with the edited answer kept; the copy-as-new ending; the dashboard search by reference; the delete confirmation page and both delete endings; the two stale-notification endings; the confirmation page's heading and the sections and links its page object names; the whole sign-in, sign-out and organisation-picker surface the auth spec proves, with its error message verbatim; organisation scoping as a rule on the backend API (403, no rows, 404 per mutation) and on a notification's page (404 Page not found); admin visibility of a submitted notification; and the hand-added commercial transporter route through to submission via Review and submit. Nine gaps record what the page objects or the slice's own shape name that no test in it drives.

claims.statement: A submitted notification's dashboard card carries an Amend button named "Amend notification <reference>", and pressing it opens that notification's review page.
claims.quote:
await this.animalsPages.dashboard.amend(referenceNumber).click();
    await this.animalsPages.notificationView.heading.waitFor(pageLoadWait);

claims.statement: Pressing Amend on a submitted notification lands on the notification-view address for that reference, tags it Amend in the journey strip, shows the reference in the strip, and shows a Cancel amend button.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/amend-endings.spec.ts:24-37 ("Amend opens the review page with the Amend tag, the reference and Cancel amend")

claims.statement: Starting an amend is a POST to the notification's amend address, which redirects to its notification-view page.
claims.note: mechanism: the seeded route the suite uses to put a notification into the amend state without walking the dashboard; CREATE_PATH is `${SET_BASES.liveAnimals}/notifications`, so the address is /live-animals/notifications/<reference>/amend.

claims.statement: A notification submitted in one browser session can be amended from a later, separate browser session: after pressing Amend there, the journey strip shows the Amend tag and the notification's reference.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/amend-from-a-later-session.spec.ts:6-17 ("amends a notification that an earlier browser session submitted")
claims.note: The strip locators are read through the Overview page object, but they are the shared journey strip, so they hold for whichever page Amend lands on: the amend action waits for the notification view (flows/animals/notification-actions.ts:41-46). Marked test.slow().

claims.statement: Amending a notification that has since been deleted is refused: the dashboard shows an Important notification banner reading "This notification could not be amended."
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/amend-from-a-later-session.spec.ts:37-51 ("tells the user a deleted notification could not be amended"), page-objects/shared/dashboard-copy.ts:1
claims.quote: await expect(freshPages.dashboard.importantBanner).toContainText(freshPages.dashboard.amendRefusedMessage);
claims.note: The message is the constant AMEND_REFUSED_MESSAGE = 'This notification could not be amended.'; importantBanner is the govuk notification banner headed 'Important' (page-objects/shared/base-page.ts:81-83).

claims.statement: A deleted notification's Amend button is still shown on its dashboard card before the delete, and the refusal only appears once it is pressed after the delete.
claims.note: It follows from the order of the test's steps: the card's Amend button is asserted visible before the delete, and the same locator is clicked after it to produce the refusal, so the stale card is still clickable.

claims.statement: An amend review with no answer yet changed is headed, and titled, "Review your notification".
claims.quote:
await expect(animalsPages.notificationView.heading).toHaveText(reviewHeadingText);
    await expect(pages.page).toHaveTitle(new RegExp(`^${reviewHeadingText}`));
claims.note: reviewHeadingText = 'Review your notification'.

claims.statement: Once an answer changes during an amend, the review's heading and page title become "Review before re-submitting".
claims.note: resubmitHeadingText = 'Review before re-submitting'. The change the test makes is the internal reference number on the origin page.

claims.statement: Adding only a document during an amend leaves the review headed and titled "Review your notification": an upload is not an answer change.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/amend-review-title.spec.ts:26-41 ("keeps the review heading when only a document is added")
claims.note: The describe block carries { tag: '@compose' }, so this one runs only against the local stack.

claims.statement: An amend review opens with no error summary on it.
claims.quote: await expect(animalsPages.notificationView.errorSummary).toHaveCount(0);
claims.note: Asserted twice: once on a freshly opened amend review, and once on an amend review whose arrival date has been cleared, so the page holds the answer error silently until Continue is pressed.

claims.statement: The notification view's level-1 heading is one of three things: the notification reference (matching GBN-[A-Z]+-\d{2}-[0-9A-Z]{6}), "Review your notification", or "Review before re-submitting".
claims.quote:
const reviewHeadings = [NOTIFICATION_REFERENCE_PATTERN, reviewHeadingText, resubmitHeadingText].join('|');
    return this.page.getByRole('main').getByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: new RegExp(`^(${reviewHeadings})$`) });
claims.note: mechanism: the page object accepts any of the three so one locator serves the draft review, the amend review and the submitted view; which one shows depends on the notification's state.

claims.statement: A question page opened from Overview while amending ends with exactly two buttons, "Save and continue" then "Save and return to overview".
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/amend-endings.spec.ts:47-52 ("ends with Save and continue beside Save and return to overview")
claims.note: The page used is arrival details, reached from the Overview task 'Arrival details'.

claims.statement: That page shows "Cancel and return to overview" as a link on its own line, entirely below the two save buttons.
claims.quote:
await expect(saveButtons.getByRole('button')).toHaveText(['Save and continue', saveAndReturnLabel]);
  await expectEntirelyAbove(saveButtons, cancelAndReturnLink);

claims.statement: A question page opened while amending shows a "Cancel amend" link in the journey strip.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/amend-endings.spec.ts:58-60 ("shows Cancel amend in the strip"), page-objects/shared/base-page.ts:281-283
claims.quote: return this.journeyStrip.getByRole('link', { name: 'Cancel amend', exact: true });

claims.statement: The Overview of an amending notification shows the Amend status tag and the strip's Cancel amend link.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/amend-endings.spec.ts:63-70 ("the strip shows Amend and Cancel amend on Overview while amending")
claims.quote:
await expect(animalsPages.overview.statusTag).toHaveText(AMEND);
    await expect(animalsPages.overview.stripCancelAmend).toBeVisible();

claims.statement: Cancel and return to overview while amending opens the Overview still tagged Amend with Cancel amend, and discards the value typed but not saved, leaving the previously saved answer in the field.
claims.note: Cancel and return to overview is a link, not a button (page-objects/shared/base-page.ts:313-315); the Overview's heading is 'Overview'.

claims.statement: A Change link on the amend review opens the page that collects that answer, carrying the review page's slug as the trail it was reached by.
claims.quote: await expectOpenFromReview(pages.page, animalsPages.originOfImport, reference, animalsPages.notificationView.slug);
claims.note: The link used is 'Change origin of import' and it opens the origin of import page with its heading visible; the trail is written as ?from=notification-view.

claims.statement: From a page opened by an amend review's Change link, Save and continue goes on to the next journey page — "What are you importing?" after the origin page — carrying the trail notification-view then origin.
claims.note: The test fills the internal reference with AMENDED_INTERNAL_REFERENCE before pressing Save and continue, so the answer has changed by then.

claims.statement: The amend review's "Change main import reason" link opens the main import reason page on the review trail, and pressing Save and continue on it and on every later page walks back to the amend review, which is still tagged Amend.
claims.note: expectSaveAndContinueWalk checks each stop is open at its exact address with the places already saved as its trail, and shows its heading, before pressing its Save and continue. The test is marked test.slow().

claims.statement: While amending, the origin of import page ends with "Save and continue" alone and shows no links in its form.
claims.quote:
await expect(animalsPages.originOfImport.formButtons).toHaveText(['Save and continue']);
    await expect(animalsPages.originOfImport.formLinks).toHaveCount(0);

claims.statement: While amending, the CPH number page ends with "Save and continue" alone, with no "Save and return to overview" button.
claims.quote:
await expect(animalsPages.cphNumber.formButtons).toHaveText(['Save and continue']);
    await expect(animalsPages.cphNumber.saveAndReturnToOverview).toHaveCount(0);

claims.statement: While amending, the permanent address page ends with "Save and continue" alone and no "Save and return to overview".
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/amend-endings.spec.ts:146-153 ("while amending, the permanent address page ends with Save and continue alone")
claims.quote:
await expect(animalsPages.permanentAddress.formButtons).toHaveText(['Save and continue']);
    await expect(animalsPages.permanentAddress.saveAndReturnToOverview).toHaveCount(0);
claims.note: This one is seeded with CAT_ANSWERS, so the permanent address page is only reachable for that commodity's answers.

claims.statement: While amending, the Amend bar's Cancel amend link on the CPH number page opens the cancel amendment confirmation page.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/amend-endings.spec.ts:155-166 ("while amending, the Amend bar’s Cancel amend opens the cancel amendment confirmation page from the CPH number page")
claims.note: This test no longer drives the contact address page: the slice proves no contact address ending or Cancel amend from it while amending.

claims.statement: The Amend bar's Cancel amend link opens the cancel amendment confirmation page from the permanent address page.
Pressing Continue on an amend review whose answers are incomplete keeps the user on the review, at the notification-view address with ?refused=1.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/amend-endings.spec.ts:182-198 ("Continue on an amend review with an answer missing stays on the review and shows There is a problem, naming what is missing")
claims.quote:
await animalsPages.notificationView.continueButton.click();

    await expect(pages.page).toHaveURL(/\/notification-view\?refused=1$/);
claims.note: The incompleteness is made by clearing the arrival date and saving and returning to the overview.

claims.statement: The refused amend review shows an error summary containing "There is a problem" whose only link reads "Complete arrival details".
claims.note: The error summary names the task to finish, not the field, so the link wording is a task name.

claims.statement: The refused amend review stays tagged Amend and does not open the Declaration page.
claims.quote:
await expect(animalsPages.notificationView.statusTag).toHaveText(AMEND);
    await expect(animalsPages.declaration.heading).not.toBeVisible();

claims.statement: A refused notification view can be opened directly at its ?refused=1 address.
claims.quote: await this.navigateToService(`${this.expectedUrl(referenceNumber)}?refused=1`);
claims.note: mechanism: the refusal state is carried in the query string rather than in the session, so the suite can open it straight away; openRefused completes sign-in if asked before waiting for the review heading.

claims.statement: While amending, the Overview and a question page both show the Amend status bar with its Cancel amend link and the reference, while the review shows a Cancel amend button instead of a link.
claims.note: stripCancelAmend is a link in the journey strip; btnCancelAmend is a button in main (page-objects/shared/base-page.ts:281-283, 297-299).

claims.statement: The Cancel amend button is shown on the review for as long as the notification is amending.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/cancel-amend-ui.spec.ts:10-13 ("shows the Cancel amend button while the notification is amending")
claims.quote:
await expect(animalsPages.notificationView.statusTag).toHaveText('Amend');
      await expect(animalsPages.notificationView.btnCancelAmend).toBeVisible();

claims.statement: Cancelling an amendment is confirmed on a page of its own at the notification's cancel-amend address, not in a dialog.
claims.quote: super(page, 'cancel-amend');
claims.note: The page object extends NotificationPage with the slug 'cancel-amend', so its address is /live-animals/notifications/<reference>/cancel-amend, and every test asserts the browser URL changed to it.

claims.statement: The cancel amendment page's level-1 heading reads "Cancel this amendment?"
claims.quote: return this.page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: 'Cancel this amendment?' });

claims.statement: The cancel amendment page explains the consequence: "Your changes since you started amending will be discarded and the submitted version restored."
The cancel amendment page offers two buttons: a confirm button reading "Yes, cancel amendment" and a reject button whose name begins No.
The cancel amendment page itself shows the Amend status tag and no Cancel amend link in its strip.
claims.quote:
await expect(animalsPages.notificationCancelAmend.statusTag).toHaveText('Amend');
      await expect(animalsPages.notificationCancelAmend.stripCancelAmend).toHaveCount(0);

claims.statement: Rejecting the cancellation returns the user to the notification view with the amendment still running: Amend tag, Cancel amend button and the Change links still present.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/cancel-amend-ui.spec.ts:65-73 ("No returns to the notification view with the amendment still in progress")

claims.statement: Cancel amend from a question page opens the confirmation page, and rejecting there returns to the notification view with the amendment kept, not to the question page.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/cancel-amend-ui.spec.ts:75-93 ("Cancel amend on a question page opens the confirmation page and Go back keeps the amendment")
claims.note: The test's title calls the reject control 'Go back' while the page object matches /No/, so the suite does not pin which word the button carries.

claims.statement: Cancel amend on the Overview opens the cancel amendment confirmation page.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/cancel-amend-ui.spec.ts:37-49 ("Cancel amend on the Overview opens the cancel-amendment confirmation page")
claims.note: Tagged { tag: '@cross-browser' }.

claims.statement: Confirming the cancellation discards the changes made since the amend started and restores the submitted answers, landing on the notification-view address with ?cancelled=1.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/cancel-amend-ui.spec.ts:109-117 ("Yes cancels the amendment and restores the submitted answers")
claims.note: Tagged { tag: '@smoke' }.

claims.statement: After cancelling, an alert on the notification view reads "The amendment has been cancelled and the submitted version restored."
claims.quote: await expect(pages.page.getByRole('alert')).toContainText('The amendment has been cancelled and the submitted version restored.');

claims.statement: After cancelling, the notification is Submitted again, with no Cancel amend button and no Change links on its view.
claims.note: The Submitted tag is read from the view header (main h1 + .govuk-tag), not the journey strip, so the submitted view carries the status beside the reference heading rather than in an amend bar.

claims.statement: Cancelling an amendment reverts an answer changed during it: the country of origin returns from Belgium to the submitted France.
claims.note: The review shows the answer in a summary list row keyed 'Country of origin'.

claims.statement: Cancel amend works with JavaScript turned off: the strip's Cancel amend on a question page, confirmed, restores the submitted answers and the Submitted status.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/cancel-amend-ui.spec.ts:122-149 ("Cancel amend without JavaScript" / "the status bar Cancel amend on a question page restores the submitted answers")
claims.quote: test.use({ javaScriptEnabled: false });
claims.note: The describe is tagged { tag: '@duplicated-in-frontend' }. The test saves Belgium on the origin page, checks the review shows Belgium, then cancels and checks ?cancelled=1, the Submitted tag, no Cancel amend button, and France restored.

claims.statement: Cancelling an amendment is a POST to the notification's cancel-amend address, which redirects to notification-view?cancelled=1.
claims.quote: await this.forms.postForm(`${CREATE_PATH}/${referenceNumber}/cancel-amend`, {}, { redirectsTo: /\/notification-view\?cancelled=1$/ });
claims.note: mechanism: the suite's seeded route to the cancelled state, matching the URL the UI test asserts.

claims.statement: Deleting a notification is confirmed on a page of its own at the notification's delete address, headed "Delete this notification?"
claims.quote:
export const deleteNotificationHeading = (page: Page): Locator =>
  page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: 'Delete this notification?' });
claims.note: The heading and confirm button come from a shared helper, so the same wording serves more than one service's delete page.

claims.statement: The delete confirmation page's confirm button reads "Yes, delete notification".
claims.quote:
export const deleteNotificationConfirm = (page: Page): Locator =>
  page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Yes, delete notification', exact: true });

claims.statement: Deleting a draft notification lands on the dashboard with a banner reading "The notification has been deleted."
claims.quote:
await animalsPages.deleteNotification.confirmDelete.click();
    await expect(animalsPages.dashboard.deletedBanner).toBeVisible();
claims.note: Tagged { tag: ['@cross-browser', '@ios'] } and marked test.slow(), inside a describe tagged { tag: '@duplicated-in-frontend' }.

claims.statement: A deleted submitted notification is gone from the dashboard: searching for its reference returns no notification cards.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/notification-delete.spec.ts:15-26 ("deletes the notification and removes it from the dashboard")
claims.note: Tagged { tag: '@smoke' }. A submitted notification can therefore be deleted, not only a draft.

claims.statement: A notification's dashboard card carries a "Delete notification <reference>" link, and following it opens the delete confirmation page.
Deleting is a soft delete: a POST to the notification's delete address that redirects to an address carrying ?deleted=1.
claims.quote: await this.forms.postForm(`${CREATE_PATH}/${referenceNumber}/delete`, {}, { redirectsTo: /\?deleted=1$/ });
claims.note: mechanism: the suite's own name for the action is softDelete, and the API client it pairs with is softDeleteNotification, so the record is kept rather than removed.

claims.statement: A notification has four statuses the suite models: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, AMEND and DELETED.
claims.note: The API values are upper case; the tags the UI shows for them read 'Draft', 'Submitted' and 'Amend'.

claims.statement: A notification's view carries a "Copy as new" button and a "Delete" button.
claims.note: No test in this part presses either: the delete and copy tests in this slice both act from the dashboard card. The page object names them, so the view offers them.

claims.statement: When the notification changed after check your answers was rendered, pressing Continue returns the user to check your answers at the notification-view address with ?staleAction=1 rather than submitting.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/declare-stale-notification.spec.ts:7-27 ("check your answers: when changed since it rendered, Continue returns to it with the current content")
claims.quote:
await animalsPages.notificationView.continueButton.click();

    await expect(pages.page).toHaveURL(/\/notification-view\?staleAction=1$/);
claims.note: The change is made by another request posting the origin form while the review page is open, standing in for another tab or another user.

claims.statement: A stale check your answers shows the message "The notification has been updated" and the notification's current content, not the content the page was rendered with.
claims.quote:
await expect(pages.page.getByText('The notification has been updated')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(pages.page.getByText(EDITED_REFERENCE)).toBeVisible();
claims.note: EDITED_REFERENCE is the internal reference the other request saved, so its presence proves the re-rendered page carries the newer answers.

claims.statement: When the notification changed after the declaration was rendered, ticking the confirmation and pressing Submit returns the user to check your answers at ?staleAction=1 with the same "The notification has been updated" message and the current content, rather than submitting.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/declare-stale-notification.spec.ts:29-52 ("declaration: when changed since it rendered, Submit returns to check your answers with the current content")

claims.statement: The review and declaration pages each carry a concurrencyToken, and a page that renders none cannot be declared against.
claims.note: mechanism: the concurrency token the form carries is how the frontend detects the stale case above. The quoted regular expression is the source's, with its named group written as a plain group here for JSON; the source reads (?<token>[^"]+).

claims.statement: The Declaration page is headed "Declaration", carries a checkbox whose label begins "I confirm that I have reviewed" and ends with a Continue button.
A successful submission lands on a confirmation page headed "Import notification submitted".
claims.quote: await expect(pages.page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Import notification submitted' })).toBeVisible();

claims.statement: An amended notification can be resubmitted, taking it Submitted then Amend then Submitted again, with the answer edited during the amend kept.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/amend-resubmit.spec.ts:6-36 ("resubmits an amended notification: Submitted → Amend → Submitted with the edited answer kept")
claims.note: The test is marked test.slow() and walks the whole journey: submit, amend from the dashboard, change the country from France to Belgium, Continue, tick the declaration, Continue, then reopen the view.

claims.statement: An amend review offers a Change link for every card: a "Change origin of import" link, a "Change commodity <commodity card title>" link, and at least four Change links in all.
claims.note: The commodity change link's name is built as `Change commodity ${commodityCardTitle(line)}` (page-objects/animals/notification-view-page.ts:84-86).

claims.statement: Once resubmitted, the notification view shows the Submitted tag, no Change links and no Cancel amend button.
A notification that has been amended and resubmitted can be amended again: its dashboard card still offers Amend.
Copying a submitted notification creates a new Draft with its own reference, which matches the notification reference pattern and differs from the original's, and leaves the original Submitted.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/amend-from-a-later-session.spec.ts:19-35 ("copies a notification that an earlier browser session submitted into a new draft and leaves the original submitted")
claims.note: Proven from a browser session later than the one that submitted the original. Copy lands the user on the copy's Overview (flows/animals/notification-actions.ts:60-66).

claims.statement: A notification's dashboard card carries, besides Amend and Delete, a "Copy as new notification <reference>" button, a "View notification <reference>" link and a "Resume notification <reference>" link, each naming its own notification.
claims.note: Each action's accessible name includes the reference, so a card's actions are distinguishable when several cards are listed. Resume and View are links; Amend and Copy as new are buttons.

claims.statement: A notification card shows its status in a Status row with a tag, so the dashboard reports Draft, Submitted or Amend per notification.
Opening the animals notification dashboard while signed out lands the user on the sign-in page.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/auth.spec.ts:14-17 ("lands on the sign in page when opening the notification dashboard")
claims.quote:
await expect(pages.page).toHaveURL(pages.signIn.expectedUrl);
    await expect(pages.signIn.heading).toBeVisible();
claims.note: The whole spec is tagged { tag: '@auth' } and runs from a cold, unauthenticated storage state: test.use({ storageState: COLD_START }).

claims.statement: The sign-in page is headed "Sign in using Government Gateway" and has a "Government Gateway user ID" textbox, a "Password" textbox and a "Sign in" button.
claims.quote: readonly headingName = 'Sign in using Government Gateway';
claims.note: The page is served by the Defra ID stub at a path ending /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp.

claims.statement: Signing in with valid credentials lands the user on the animals dashboard at /live-animals, headed "Import notification service".
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/auth.spec.ts:19-23 ("allows signing into the notification dashboard"), page-objects/animals/dashboard-page.ts:14-18, page-objects/shared/sets.ts:2
claims.note: Tagged { tag: ['@smoke', '@cross-browser'] }. The dashboard's address is the live animals set base, '/live-animals'.

claims.statement: Signing in with an invalid user id keeps the user on the sign-in page and shows an error summary containing "Enter a valid 10-digit customer reference number (CRN) and password".
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/auth.spec.ts:25-29 ("displays an error message when signing in with invalid user id")
claims.quote: await expect(pages.signIn.errorSummary).toContainText('Enter a valid 10-digit customer reference number (CRN) and password');

claims.statement: Signing in with an invalid password gives the same error, on the same page: the message does not say which of the two was wrong.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/auth.spec.ts:31-35 ("displays an error message when signing in with invalid password")

claims.statement: The service root redirects a signed-in user to the default set's dashboard, /live-animals.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/auth.spec.ts:37-42 ("redirects the service root to the default set’s dashboard")
claims.note: Live animals is therefore the default of the three sets the suite knows: liveAnimals, highRiskPlants and germinalProducts (page-objects/shared/sets.ts:1-5).

claims.statement: A signed-in user can sign out: the dashboard carries a "Log out" link whose href is /auth/sign-out, and following it lands on a page headed "You have signed out".
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/auth.spec.ts:44-50 ("allows signing out after signing in"), page-objects/shared/base-page.ts:65-67, page-objects/shared/auth/sign-out-page.ts:3-12
claims.note: The link's wording is 'Log out' while the page it reaches says 'You have signed out', and the path is /auth/sign-out: the service uses both words. The signed-out page is on the Defra ID host, at a path matching /idphub/b2c/b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi/signout.

claims.statement: The signed-in user's email address is not shown on the dashboard.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/auth.spec.ts:52-55 ("does not display the signed in user after signing in"), page-objects/shared/base-page.ts:61-63
claims.quote: await expect(animalsPages.dashboard.user()).toHaveCount(0);
claims.note: user() defaults to the default identity's email address, so the assertion is that that text appears nowhere on the page.

claims.statement: Reopening the notification dashboard after signing out lands on the sign-in page again: the session does not survive sign-out.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/auth.spec.ts:57-64 ("lands on the sign in page when reopening the notification dashboard after sign out")

claims.statement: A page part-way through the journey is protected: with the journey's own cookies kept but the session cookie cleared, reopening the origin page of a started notification lands on the sign-in page.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/auth.spec.ts:66-85 ("Origin of the import (unauthenticated entry)" / "lands on the sign in page when opening a page further in the journey")
claims.note: mechanism: the journey's own cookies are named with the set prefix 'liveAnimals', separate from the auth session cookie, so the test can drop one and keep the other.

claims.statement: Signing in from a page part-way through the journey returns the user to that same page, at /live-animals/notifications/<reference>/origin.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/auth.spec.ts:87-91 ("allows signing into a page further in the journey")
claims.quote:
await expect(pages.page).toHaveURL(new RegExp(`${SET_BASES.liveAnimals}/notifications/${referenceNumber}/origin$`));
      await expect(animalsPages.originOfImport.heading).toBeVisible();

claims.statement: The dashboard starts a notification from a button reading "Start a new notification", which opens the origin page of a new notification with its reference in the address.
claims.quote:
await animalsPages.dashboard.btnCreateNewNotification.click();
      referenceNumber = animalsPages.originOfImport.referenceNumberFromUrl();

claims.statement: A failed sign-in shows a page headed "Sorry, we are unable to sign you in." carrying a "try again" link, and signing in a second time from it either succeeds or raises the same failure.
claims.quote: readonly headingName = 'Sorry, we are unable to sign you in.';
claims.note: mechanism: the suite retries once through the 'try again' link and throws 'Sign-in failed twice' if the error page comes back, so a single transient sign-in failure does not fail a test.

claims.statement: An identity with more than one organisation is asked to choose one after sign-in, on a page headed "Choose your organisation" with a radio per organisation whose name ends "SBI <sbi>" and a Continue button.
claims.quote:
/**
 * defra-id-stub's "Choose your organisation" screen, shown after sign-in only
 * for identities with more than one organisation (POST /organisations, radio
 * value keyed by sbi).
 */
claims.note: Driven in this part by the organisation-scoped notification page test, which signs a second identity in with an explicit organisationSbi. Signing in without naming one, when the picker appears, raises 'Signed-in identity has more than one organisation but no organisationSbi was provided to select one.' (page-objects/shared/base-page.ts:239-249).

claims.statement: The suite signs in with two identities: a default single-organisation identity (CRN 2100010101, organisation 5900001) and a second identity (CRN 2100010102) belonging to two organisations, SBI 110100101 and SBI 110100102.
claims.note: The CRNs and organisations mirror trade-imports-defra-id-stub's mock data. The sign-in password comes from the environment with a hard-coded fallback: [REDACTED].

claims.statement: A user of another organisation reading a submitted notification's fulfilments on the backend API is refused with HTTP 403.
claims.quote: await expectRefusalWith(() => otherOrganisationNotificationApi.getNotificationFulfilments(draft.referenceNumber), 403);

claims.statement: A user of another organisation listing notifications by a reference they do not own gets no rows back: the total is zero, not a refusal.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/organisation-scoped-notifications.spec.ts:17-27 ("returns no rows when another organisation lists by reference")
claims.quote:
const totalElements = await otherOrganisationNotificationApi.countNotifications(draft.referenceNumber);
    expect(totalElements).toBe(0);
claims.note: The list is filtered rather than refused, so another organisation cannot tell from a list whether a reference exists.

claims.statement: A user of another organisation is refused with HTTP 404 on every change to a notification: amend, save, submit, copy, soft delete and cancel amend.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/organisation-scoped-notifications.spec.ts:29-46 ("returns 404 when another organisation mutates a notification")
claims.note: 404, not 403, for a change: the notification is reported as absent rather than forbidden. The six named actions are the whole set of changes the notification API offers.

claims.statement: The organisation a request acts for is carried on the backend API in a Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header.
claims.quote: export const ORGANISATION_ID_HEADER = 'Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id';

claims.statement: The organisation scoping tests use organisation id 9999999 as the other organisation, against the default identity's organisation 5900001.
claims.quote:
export const E2E_ORGANISATION_ID = defaultUser.organisationId;
export const OTHER_ORGANISATION_ID = '9999999';

claims.statement: A signed-in user of another organisation who opens a notification's page by its address is shown the 404 Page not found page.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/organisation-scoped-notification-page.spec.ts:7-26 ("shows page not found and none of the notification"), page-objects/shared/page-not-found.ts:3-6
claims.note: The page's level-1 heading is the number 404 and 'Page not found' appears as body text beneath it.

claims.statement: That refusal leaks nothing about the notification: neither its Overview heading nor its reference number appears on the page.

The other-organisation page refusal is proven with a real second sign-in: a fresh cold browser context signs the second identity in by CRN and picks its own organisation's SBI before opening the address.
claims.note: Signing in as another user from an already-signed-in context is refused by the suite with a message telling the author to start cold instead (page-objects/shared/base-page.ts:224-237).

claims.statement: A notification submitted in the animals journey is listed in the admin app and can be found there by its reference, in a table row.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/admin-visibility.spec.ts:11-23 ("a notification submitted in the animals journey is listed in the admin app")
claims.note: Tagged { tag: '@animals-admin' } and marked test.slow(). The notification is only looked up, never deleted.

claims.statement: The admin app reads notifications through animals-backend, so an operator finding a submitted notification there proves the journey app and the admin app agree on what the journey wrote.
claims.quote:
/**
 * Integration seam: an operator in the admin app can find what a user submitted in the animals journey.
 *
 * The admin app reads notifications through animals-backend, so this proves the two apps agree on the
 * notification the journey wrote. The notification is only looked up, never deleted: the admin domain's
 * own specs cover the delete actions.
 */

claims.statement: A trader can submit a notification whose transporter is a commercial transporter they added by hand rather than chose from a list.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/commercial-transporter-submission.spec.ts:5-36 ("a trader can submit a notification using a hand-added commercial transporter")
claims.note: Tagged { tag: '@cross-browser' } and marked test.slow().

claims.statement: The hand-added commercial transporter is reached from the Overview task "Transport details", then the transporter page's Add transporter control, then choosing the transporter type "Commercial" and pressing Continue.
The add-a-commercial-transporter page is headed "Add a commercial transporter" and sits at the notification's transporters/add/commercial address.

The add-a-commercial-transporter page asks for a Transporter authorisation number, Name or organisation name, Address line 1, Town or city, Postcode or Zip code, Country, Email address and Phone number.
claims.note: The suite's fill() enters every field except Country, so Country is the one field the hand-added transporter path does not set in this part's test.

claims.statement: Each hand-added commercial transporter the suite creates gets a name made unique with a random suffix, so repeated runs do not collide on an existing transporter.
claims.note: mechanism: the suite appends eight characters of a UUID to the canned transporter's name so the same test can run many times against one environment.

claims.statement: Transited countries are added one at a time on their own page and saved with "Save and return to overview"; the submission journey adds France and Belgium.
claims.note: The test seeds a partial draft and resumes it in the browser on the transited countries page before adding the two countries.

claims.statement: Submission runs Overview, then the review, then the Declaration: pressing Continue on the review opens the Declaration, and ticking the confirmation and pressing Continue there submits.
claims.note: The same three steps end both a first submission and a resubmission after an amend.

claims.statement: An amending notification's answers are reached and saved through the same journey pages as a draft's, and the Amend state is carried in the page's own status bar rather than in a separate set of pages.
claims.quote: test('while amending, the origin page and the CPH number page end with Save and continue alone', async ({
claims.note: It follows from every amend test opening the ordinary page addresses (originOfImport, cphNumber, permanentAddress, arrivalDetails, overview) and finding the Amend tag and Cancel amend in the shared journey strip, with only the page endings differing from a draft's.

claims.statement: A notification's reference number follows the pattern GBN-<letters>-<two digits>-<six letters or digits>.
claims.quote: export const NOTIFICATION_REFERENCE_PATTERN = 'GBN-[A-Z]+-\\d{2}-[0-9A-Z]{6}';

claims.statement: A submitted notification's view carries a date submitted, a date created, an "Amend this notification" button and an "Import reference numbers" region, read from the view header rather than the amend strip.
claims.quote: /** The header of a notification's view, in every status that has one: reference, statusTag, dateCreated or dateSubmitted, actions and import reference numbers. */
claims.note: No test in this part asserts these: the amend tests in this slice start the amend from the dashboard card, not from the view's 'Amend this notification' button. The page object names them, so the submitted view offers them.

claims.statement: Each test's reference numbers are recorded against the test run, so a failed amend, cancel or delete can be traced to the notification it acted on.
claims.note: mechanism: the suite's own diagnostics, not service behaviour.

claims.statement: A later browser session is a new browser context carrying only the signed-in session cookie, so a test proves what a user sees on returning rather than what the first session's journey state held.
claims.quote: /** The yar `session` cookie carries per-user journey state that would bleed across a worker's tests. */
claims.note: mechanism: stripToAuthCookie keeps only the auth cookie when the fresh context is opened, which is what makes the later-session amend, copy and delete tests meaningful.

claims.statement: The signed-in session is held in a cookie named sid, with per-service names ins-sid and plants-sid when the services run on the local stack.
claims.note: The services share the localhost cookie domain but keep separate session-store prefixes, so a session minted against one is not valid against the others (fixtures/auth-state.ts:76-79).

claims.statement: The animals service's landing page after sign-in is its dashboard at the service root.
claims.quote: animals: { landingPath: '/', landingHeading: (page) => new AnimalsDashboardPage(page).heading },
claims.note: The INS service lands on /address-book instead, and animals-admin and plants on their own roots.

claims.statement: The suite does not say what the delete confirmation page warns beyond its heading: no test and no page object names any body copy on it.
claims.note: Looked in both delete page objects and both delete tests: only the level-1 heading and the confirm button are named. The cancel amendment page, by contrast, has its consequence sentence asserted verbatim. There is also no reject or cancel control named for the delete page.

claims.statement: The suite does not pin the wording of the cancel amendment page's reject button.
claims.note: The locator matches any button whose name contains No, and the one test title that names the control calls it 'Go back', so the suite proves a reject control exists and where it leads but not what it reads.

claims.statement: No test in this slice proves what a stale notification does on an amend review: both stale tests act on a draft at check your answers and at the declaration.
claims.note: Looked through both tests in declare-stale-notification.spec.ts and every amend spec in this part: the ?staleAction=1 ending is only proven for a draft, so whether an amend review refuses the same way is unproven here.

claims.statement: No test in this slice proves that cancelling an amendment restores anything other than a changed answer: a document added during the amend, or a commodity added or removed, is not covered.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/cancel-amend-ui.spec.ts:96-149 (both restoring tests change only the country of origin)
claims.note: Looked at both tests that press Yes, cancel amendment, and at amend-review-title.spec.ts, which uploads a document during an amend but never cancels. What a cancel does to an upload made during the amend is unproven.

claims.statement: No test in this slice proves what a notification's own view shows once it has been deleted: only the dashboard's refusal banner and the card's disappearance are covered.
claims.note: Looked in both delete tests and the deleted-amend refusal test. Whether opening a deleted notification's address shows a 404, a Deleted status or the old content is not asserted anywhere in this part, although DELETED is one of the four statuses the suite models.

claims.statement: No test in this slice proves a refusal message body or problem detail for the organisation-scoped API refusals: only the status codes are asserted.
claims.note: expectRefusalWith checks the error is a RestClientError and its status, and returns the error, but neither organisation-scoping test reads anything from it. What the API says in the body of a 403 or 404 is unproven here.

claims.statement: No test in this slice proves the sign-in error for an empty user id or an empty password, only for values that are present but invalid.
claims.note: Both error tests pass the literal 'invalid'. Whether a blank field gives the same message, or names the missing field, is unproven in this part.

claims.statement: No test in this slice drives the organisation picker as a journey of its own: no test signs in with the two-organisation identity, reads the picker's heading and options and then switches organisation.
claims.note: Looked through auth.spec.ts and organisation-scoped-notification-page.spec.ts: the picker is only passed through by naming an SBI up front, so its heading, its radio labels and what happens when a user picks the other organisation are unproven. The spec that does use it is proving scoping, not the picker.

claims.statement: No test in this slice proves that another organisation's user is refused a notification's view page as well as its Overview page.
claims.note: The one UI scoping test opens the Overview address of a started draft. Whether the notification-view, declaration, cancel-amend and delete addresses refuse the same way is covered only on the API, by status code.

claims.statement: The Overview carries a "Review and submit" button, and pressing it opens the notification's review page.
claims.quote: return this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Review and submit' });
claims.note: Driven in this slice by the commercial transporter submission test, after the transporter is saved back to the Overview.

claims.statement: The submission confirmation page has a section headed "Before the consignment is imported" listing outstanding items, and a section headed "How to view or amend this notification" with a sentence beneath it.
claims.quote: return this.page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Before the consignment is imported' }).locator('~ ul').first().getByRole('listitem');
claims.note: The page object names both headings, the list and the sentence; no test in this slice asserts them, the specs here check only the 'Import notification submitted' heading. The second heading's locator reads getByRole('heading', { name: 'How to view or amend this notification' }).

claims.statement: The submission confirmation page links to "contact HMRC (opens in a new tab)" and "Find out about call charges (opens in a new tab)".
claims.quote: return this.page.getByRole('link', { name: 'contact HMRC (opens in a new tab)', exact: true });
claims.note: Named by the page object only; no test in this slice follows either link.

claims.statement: The animals dashboard finds a notification by its reference: the user types it into the "Keyword or reference" field and presses Search, and the address then carries it as referenceNumber.
claims.quote: this.page.waitForURL((url) => (url.searchParams.get('referenceNumber') ?? '') === referenceNumber),
claims.note: The field and button sit in the form with test id notification-search-form.
